appearances.snippet: There was a man named Mark A. Liti, and he died in a rather bizarre accident. records.text: Owens said the prosecution relied on Pennsylvania cases involving one death, but she argued those cases involved an intent to kill multiple people that circumstances prevented.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: But we'd like to borrow from Pennsylvania law. This is what they're actually arguing. Pennsylvania law and their jurisprudence does meet this standard. ... And so they in their response to the dismissal are citing cases in Pennsylvania where there was just one victim and it was enough as an aggravating factor. ... But these were actually extremely special cases where actually the clear intention was for there to be more than one victim, but fate sort of intervened and prevented that from occurring. ... So somebody sprayed a bunch of bullets at kids, but only one of the kids got hit and died. That's one example of a case that they looked at. ... So they brought the aggravating factor because if this man had gotten his way, more children would have been dead.
